name: Rehoboam
description: King living at the time of United Monarchyand Divided Monarchy

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon and his wisdom are written in the book of the acts of Solomon; he reigned in Jerusalem over Israel forty years, then slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Rehoboam consulted with the old men that stood before Solomon his father: how do ye advise that I may answer this people? But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him: those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men, how do you advise that I may answer this people; to the young men, what counsel give ye that we may answer this people? Meaning we all together, y'all my peers, we running this thing.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with.

Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him.

note.label: 1 Kings 12: The Kingdom Divided Under Rehoboam and Jeroboam

points: In Judah, Rehoboam, forty-one at his accession, reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and Judah did evil and provoked the Most High to jealousy above all their fathers.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: In Rehoboam's fifth year, Shishak king of Egypt comes against Jerusalem and takes the treasures of the house of the Most High and the king's house, including the gold shields Solomon made.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: There is continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam, and when Rehoboam dies, Abijam his son reigns in his place.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years, then sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and his son Rehoboam reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 9: The Queen of Sheba and the Glory of Solomon

points: Rehoboam tells them to come again after three days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam first takes counsel with the old men who stood before Solomon while his father lived, asking what answer to return.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: Rehoboam still reigns over the children of Israel who dwell in the cities of Judah, but when he sends Hadoram over the tribute, Israel stones him to death.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

points: When Rehoboam comes to Jerusalem he gathers a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors of Judah and Benjamin to fight against Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Rehoboam dwells in Jerusalem and builds cities for defense in Judah, including Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, Bethzur, Hebron, and others.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Rehoboam takes Mahalath and Abihail as wives who bear him children, then takes Maachah the daughter of Absalom, whom he loves above all his wives and concubines.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: When Rehoboam establishes the kingdom and strengthens himself, he forsakes the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: In the fifth year of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem because Rehoboam transgressed against the Lord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah gathered at Jerusalem and declares the word of the Lord: because they have forsaken him, he has left them in the hand of Shishak.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place and commits them to the guard that keeps the entrance of the king's house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns; he is forty and one years old when he begins to reign and reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord chose to put his name there.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: The acts of Rehoboam are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies, and there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, is buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Vain men, the children of Belial, gathered to Jeroboam and strengthened themselves against Rehoboam when he was young and tenderhearted and could not withstand them.
Young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

cases.name: Rehoboam
cases.charge: Forsaking the counsel of the old men for the young men he grew up with; and forsaking the law of the Lord when the kingdom was established
cases.preview: All Israel came to Shechem to make Solomon’s son king and asked him to lighten the heavy yoke his father had laid on them (1 Kings 12:1-4).
